standfirst: Betaretrovirus carries the only separate protease ORF in the family. Where the other three modules fold protease into pol, here pro is its own reading frame between gag and pol, deposited 94 times. The module also carries Rem, an RNA export protein the deposited vocabulary never names once.

modules.Betaretrovirus: pro is declared on evidence, not convention: testing the module's own naming rules before the generic subunit rule is what kept its 94 deposits together. Treating “protease” as a pol cleavage product — which it is in the other three modules — would have cut the collection to a quarter of its evidence. REM is called by get_splice_variant_features.pl from references whose coding sequence crosses one intron; it never takes copy_num.

gaps: REM's overall rate is low and the denominator is the reason. Rem exists in the MMTV clade and nowhere else in the genus, and it fires in every MMTV-group genome of the held-out panel — 100% inside the clade. Its overlap with ENV is real MMTV architecture, since rem shares the envelope signal-peptide exon, and is declared expected rather than suppressed. REM is also the clearest case in this family of a feature the strings could never have found: zero deposits anywhere in the genus name it.
